name: CHIPS
summary: CHIPS was a Minnesota research programme testing whether water-Cherenkov neutrino detectors could be built economically inside flooded mine pits. Its deployed large prototype suffered problems that prevented neutrino data taking.
detection_principle: A light-tight container held purified water and photomultiplier detector planes within a flooded mine pit. The surrounding water supplied buoyant mechanical support and cosmic-ray shielding. Timing with the NuMI beam was designed to select beam-neutrino interactions.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The final design and DAQ publications describe a completed R&D project and explain that deployment problems prevented neutrino data taking.

timeline.event: Large prototype deployed in the mine pit; later deployment and operational problems prevented the intended exposure.
Final apparatus and DAQ reports published.

key_parameters.name: Readout strategy
key_parameters.value: Modular PMT arrays with locally generated high voltage and synchronized electronics

results.summary: Demonstrated construction, instrumentation and commissioning concepts. No neutrino-oscillation or neutrino-cross-section measurement was obtained with the deployed large prototype.
